title: THE HUMANS plays through Nov. 14 at Redtwist Theatre in Chicago. #the...
transcript: yesterday I visited my old stomping grounds In Andersonville — one of my favorite neighborhoods in Chicago the area’s change a lot over the years but my favorites were still there including The Brown Elephant and Women and Children's First book store but the reason for the trip is to visit one of my favorite store front theaters in Chicago Redtwist — and to see their production of Stephen Karam’s “The Humans.” Now I consider Chicago’s storefront scene to be the backbone of the city's cultural landscape and Redtwist is quintessential storefront. it's scrappy and intimate with outstanding acting by deeply experience Chicago talent “The Humansl leans into Redtwist’s strengths of ensemble acting and this ensemble was tight not a weak link now this is a hard show to describe because it's deceptively complex… on the surface it's a play about family dynamics told through a housewarming slash thanksgiving meal but it's really about big ideas such as love, loss, forgiveness and deep generational pain. It says all of this without feeling preachy or forced and there's a moment when the family reads a note from the grandmother that had me silently weeping in the corner of their living room. yes in this production you sit in the playing space. can't recommend enough — go see it.
